patterns.title: Rewrite the Nightmare
patterns.short_description: Revise a recurring nightmare while awake and rehearse the changed version.
use_when: A recurring nightmare returns to the same threat or helpless ending.
The dream feels manageable enough to approach while awake.
goals: Practice alternative imagery without forcing an immediate change in sleep.
mechanisms: Imagery rescripting and waking rehearsal; the precise clinical mechanism remains debated.
patterns.difficulty: Introductory, with clinical support when distress is overwhelming
patterns.estimated_practice_time: 10–15 minutes to draft; 10–20 minutes of daytime rehearsal (timer defaults to 10 minutes)
prerequisites: One nightmare that feels manageable to approach while awake.
not_ideal_when: Engaging with the dream causes overwhelming distress, dissociation, or worsening symptoms.
example_user_queries: I keep having the same nightmare. Is there anything I can do while awake?
My dream always ends with me trapped and helpless.
I wake up frightened by a dream that keeps coming back.
Can I change how a recurring nightmare ends?
I keep dreaming that something is chasing me.
How can I rehearse a less frightening version of a dream?
Do I have to understand what a nightmare means before changing it?
I cannot visualize clearly. Can I still work with a recurring dream?

visual_decision.reason: The supplied corridor example and concise process line already explain the sequence; no additional illustration is needed.
